title: (RHBA-2016:1467) Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise atomic-openshift-utils bug fix update
portal_summary: Updated atomic-openshift-utils and openshift-ansible packages that fix several bugs are now available for Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise.
portal_synopsis: Red Hat OpenShift Enterprise atomic-openshift-utils bug fix update
portal_product_filter: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform|Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform|3.2|x86_64
portal_solution:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata relevant to your system have been applied.

To apply this update, run the following on all hosts where you intend to initiate Ansible-based installation or upgrade procedures:

# yum update atomic-openshift-utils

This update is available via the Red Hat Network. Details on how to use the Red Hat Network to apply this update are available at https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258.
portal_description:
OpenShift Enterprise by Red Hat is the company's cloud computing Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) solution designed for on-premise or private cloud deployments.

The atomic-openshift-utils and openshift-ansible packages contain the installation utility and Ansible requirements for installing and upgrading OpenShift Enterprise 3.

This update fixes the following bugs:

* Previously, the upgrade playbooks only supported upgrading from OpenShift Enterprise (OSE) 3.1 to 3.2. This bug fix updates the upgrade playbooks to support 3.2 minor upgrades in addition to major upgrades from 3.1. The upgrade playbook has been renamed from v3_1_to_v3_2 to v3_2 and may be used for both scenarios. (BZ#1356301)

* A recent update to the installer renamed the variable used to set the registry's selector from `openshift_registry_selector` to `openshift_hosted_registry_selector`. This bug fix adds backwards compatibility with the old variable name so that either may be used. (BZ#1344302)

* Previously, setting a default node selector prevented successful deployment of the router and registry components if those components did not match the default node selector as well. This bug fix updates the installer to ensure the selectors provided for the router and registry override the default node selectors, ensuring proper deployment. (BZ#1348518)

* If using proxy settings, re-running the config playbook to maintain an OpenShift Enterprise environment restarted Docker multiple times on all masters and nodes without doing any proper evacuation. This bug fix updates the config playbook to handle proxy settings appropriately when re-run. (BZ#1347303)

* The installer previously only took into consideration the first selector when computing the registry replica count, which could cause the registry to be created with an incorrect replica count. This bug fix ensures that the entire selector is now used when determining the replica count for registry deployment. As a result, the registry is now configured with the correct replica count based on the number of nodes that match the full selector. (BZ#1328464)

* A formatting error in the uninstall playbook caused certain tasks to be skipped. This bug fix corrects the formatting error, ensuring all tasks are completed. (BZ#1351402)

* Previously, the node may have been configured to use dnsmasq without ensuring that dnsmasq was started. The installation playbook now ensures that dnsmasq is started. (BZ#1352757)

* If no NFS storage was specified when installing OpenShift Enterprise, the integrated Docker registry was not deployed by default. This bug fix updates the installation process to deploy a registry in this scenario with an emptyDir volume by default if infrastructure nodes are present. (BZ#1316868)

All OpenShift Enterprise 3 users are advised to upgrade to these updated packages.
